title: Resolve tokenizer-shard synchronization causing intermittent TTFT pauses across deployments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Customer-facing incidents (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported intermittent first-token pauses and elevated TTFT for several models after the recent model compile/variant promotion. Impact pattern: short (200-900ms) pauses ~every 5-20 requests for affected tenants; tokens/sec downstream remained normal once stream resumed. Triage indicates the pauses correlate with request batches that span tokenizer-shard boundaries on the router side when a model variant swap occurs.

Root cause hypothesis: the router's tokenizer-shard affinity handshake does not include a compact epoch/sequence check. When a model variant is compiled or kernel set changes, tokenizer shard mappings (shard ids -> tokenizer instance) are briefly inconsistent between router and worker leading to a synchronous repair path: router queues the stream until shards reconcile, causing TTFT pause. This is exacerbated by multi-variant fanout and by private clusters with slow catalog update cadence.

Work completed so far: reproduced locally with the stress harness (token-shard-inconsistency scenario), added deterministic repro job that triggers after variant swap. Implemented a proof-of-concept patch that: (1) adds a lightweight epoch tag to tokenizer-shard metadata in the handshake; (2) enables immediate graceful fallback to single-stream, single-shard processing when mismatch detected (avoids waiting for full reconciliation); (3) emits detailed telemetry events when fallback occurs.

Planned fix: push the epoch-tag + fallback patch to runtime router (canary), add config flag runtime.router.tokenizer_shard_epoch=true for safe rollout. Canary plan: enable on Dedicated pool first (small set of tenants) for 4 hours, validate TTFT and fallback rate <0.1%. If stable, enable hosted canary (5% of traffic) then staged rollout to hosted and Private (via config bundle). Private clusters: provide opt-in bundle and a short runbook for operators to deploy and verify.

Monitoring: created Grafana dashboard with first-byte and TTFT broken down by fallback status and by shard-mismatch events. Alert rule: page on >1% tenants with TTFT delta >250ms for 10m.

Customer comms: drafted escalation message for affected accounts with mitigation steps and ETA for canary start.

Risks and mitigations: fallback mode increases per-request CPU on router; we measured ~3% CPU increase at canary load—will monitor. Also need coordination with build/release for variant metadata schema bump (backwards compatible).

Next steps: finalize code review, CI runs, deploy canary to Dedicated (target 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC), run 4-hour validation, then staged rollout. Update runbook with rollback steps and private cluster operator instructions.
